newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka buys 0.5-pct diesel for Trincomalee use.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka buys 0.5-pct diesel for Trincomalee use.

text.p: Sri Lanka is seeking low sulphur diesel in its latest tender because of demand from the northern town of Trincomalee, which uses "super diesel" for transport, a senior official at state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) said.
"We have created some ullage at Trincomalee and that is why we tendered for 0.5 percent diesel," the official said.
Sri Lanka usually buys 1.0 percent sulphur diesel in tenders that are issued every two to four weeks.
The official said that as consumption at Trincomalee is very small it does not reguarly issue tenders for the purchase of 0.5 percent sulfur diesel.
He said Trincomalee's diesel consumption is about 100 tonnes per day compared with Colombo's 2,800 tonnes. Also Trincomalee has storage capacity for between three to four months of demand.
The last time CPC issued a 0.5-percent sulphur tender for gas oil was in March, the official said.

CPC's tender for the purchase of 160,000 barrels of diesel and 40,000 barrels of jet fuel for delivery to Colombo and Trincomalee on November 24-25 closes on October 30 with offers valid to November 1.
